title: Beyond the fit: what clinicians should look for in an anti-snoring appliance
html:
Mark Orridge shares his expert advice for selecting the right anti-snoring appliance, taking into account the patient, clinician and technician.

Choosing an anti-snoring appliance involves more than selecting a device. Patients want comfort and value, clinicians want a reliable fit, and dental technicians want a practical design that can be manufactured consistently. Bringing those priorities together is where an experienced laboratory partner makes a difference.

DB Digital Laboratory, the in-house laboratory at DB Orthodontics, can provide the MSi Mandibular Snoring Inhibitor to clinicians throughout the UK. Combining the appliance’s thoughtful design with specialist technical knowledge and direct communication, our team helps all types of dental practices offer a bespoke solution for suitable patients.

Understanding the patient behind the prescription

Dental technician and MSi designer Phil Chapman identified a familiar challenge: an appliance that works well for some patients, may be difficult for others to tolerate. Bruxism, dry mouth, restricted nasal breathing, sensitivity or bulky components can all influence appliance choice and everyday use.

A patient may mention some of these concerns, but others can be overlooked. For example, someone who grinds their teeth during sleep may be unaware of the habit. Careful assessment and communication between the patient, clinician and the laboratory therefore remain essential.

Not all appliances are suitable for everyone. Where symptoms suggest obstructive sleep apnoea, appropriate assessment and a referral should form part of the clinical pathway. For patients considered suitable for a mandibular advancement appliance, the MSi offers features designed to address several practical barriers to regular wear.

Designed with comfort and regular use in mind

Patient compliance begins with an appliance people feel they can wear. The MSi’s slim, low-profile construction is designed to limit bulk, while its provision for lateral movement allows greater freedom than a rigid restricted design.

Its design avoids cheek-side linkage arms and allows the mouth to open or close during wear. These details matter when discussing comfort, breathing and dry mouth for patients. They should be considered alongside everyone’s clinical needs, rather than treated as a guarantee of suitability.

Accessible components also make cleaning straightforward. Giving patients clear guidance on cleaning, handling and any adjustments helps them understand how to care for their appliance and use it as prescribed.

Strength and adjustment for everyday demands

Durability was central to Phil’s design. The MSi incorporates a robust hook and support arrangement designed to withstand the demands of heavy bruxism. Its replaceable components also support long-term maintenance.

The adjustable mechanism enables mandibular advancement to be achieved within the appliance’s available range. Patients can adjust when needed, under their clinician’s instructions, helping balance comfort with the correct advancement position. Follow-up appointments remain important to review tolerance, appliance condition and treatment response.

The dedicated Bite Right registration tool supports the recording of the protrusive bite. Combined with accurate records and a clear prescription, this helps establish the correct starting point for the laboratory to manufacture.

The expertise behind your appliance

At DB Digital Laboratory, technology enhances experience; it does not replace it. Our team brings more than three decades of specialist orthodontic laboratory experience to its work.

Our technicians, designers and laboratory specialists collaborate with clinicians to understand the requirements behind each prescription. That approach underpins our broader portfolio, from digitally planned expander appliances to mesialisers and distalisers, and informs the support available to practices requesting the MSi.

For clinicians, the benefit is direct access to a team that understands appliance construction and the practical questions that may arise during treatment. Discussing records, design considerations or maintenance with the laboratory helps keep communication clear and decisions informed.

From prescription to precision

Every case starts with clinical information needed to manufacture each appliance. Within DB Digital Laboratory, prescriptions and accompanying records are reviewed for completeness, with any queries raised before production proceeds. This early communication helps reduce avoidable delays and ensures the team understands what the clinician requires.

Our digital laboratory workflow includes preparing STL files and producing models using advanced 3D printing. For an MSi case, the team can advise on the information and bite registration required and discuss the suitable submission route.

Careful manufacture, quality control and dispatch complete the process. Throughout, our focus is on supporting the prescribing clinician with an appliance made for each individual patient.
